scope: A reaction emoji removed from a message could never be added again: the store discarded every later add for a tombstoned (messageId, reactor, emoji) triple, so the re-add showed only locally. Decided 2026-10-17: add wins iff strictly newer than the removal.

behavior.model: Last-writer-wins register per (messageId, reactor, emoji) triple, ONE row per triple: createdAt = newest add ms, removedAt = newest removal ms (both folded with max). Live iff createdAt (floored to the second) > removedAt; ties go to removal. Legacy tombstone (removed, no removedAt) => removal wins.
behavior.inbound_removal: Emoji-tagged removals are always remembered: raise removedAt on the triple's row, or insert a hidden removal-only tombstone (createdAt 0, removed true) when no row exists. Untagged removals keep the old single-candidate semantics (not remembered; documented limit).
behavior.inbound_add: Raises createdAt with max(); revives iff newer than removedAt. eventId is taken only by the id-matching optimistic row or by an add not older than the row's add second, never on a removed row, so a stale echo cannot take over a pending re-add.
behavior.optimistic: applyOptimistic merges into the triple's existing row (keeping removedAt, createdAt bumped past the removal second); applyOptimisticRemoval sets removedAt=max(now, createdAt); rollbackOptimistic of a merged re-add returns the row to its tombstone.

constraints: No migration: removedAt optional, legacy rows keep removal-wins
No new publish; privacy invariant untouched
non_goals: Sub-second precision of removal vs re-add on peers (documented same-second limit)
Reordering removal-before-any-add (a removal with no matching row is still discarded, as before)
remediation_round_1: Reviewer rejected round 0: 9 of 24 arrival orders of a1,r1,a2,r2 ended wrong, and a late a1 echo took over the re-add's eventId. Replaced the tombstone-revive logic by the LWW model above.
